summary: SGLang main already pins FlashInfer 0.6.18, whose tagged source contains the issue-specific +1 route-map padding workaround merged in FlashInfer PR 4288. No duplicate SGLang operator change was justified. This is source/dependency verification; the original SM100 runtime failure was not reproduced on the assigned gfx950 GPU.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before source boundary: FlashInfer v0.6.12 has unpadded route-map allocations and does not contain all three +1 safeguards.
Passing-after source boundary: FlashInfer v0.6.18 pads the common launcher and both independent routing metadata entry points and has no legacy unpadded route-map assignment.
The assigned device is one AMD Instinct MI350X with gfx950 ISA, not an NVIDIA SM100/B200 device.

gpu_execution_evidence: The only assigned GPU is AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 under ROCm 7.2. The defect is in a CUDA SM100 FlashInfer cubin, which cannot execute on this GPU; FlashInfer is not installed in the prepared ROCm environment.
remaining_limitations: No NVIDIA B200/SM100 GPU was available, so the CUDA illegal-memory-access behavior and the corrected cubin were not executed.
GLM-5.2-NVFP4 weights and the original crash dump were unavailable.
The reported TP=8, speculative decoding, hierarchical cache, and production serving workload were not reproduced on the single assigned GPU.
The audit verifies the dependency pin and tagged integration workaround, not semantic accuracy or full-model stability.
